problem: Find the global maximum of the function $f(x,y)={x}^{3}-{y}^{2}+2y-1$ on the closed square $D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1}.$ You're given that $f$ has a critical point at $(0,1),$ and on the boundary of the square the points that could give rise to extreme values are the vertices.

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Global Extrema of Multivariable Functions
